- When sentiment is consistently negative or neutral over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% of recent range.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 3–5% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model often underestimates upside; add 1–3% buffer to forecast if recent sentiment >0.5.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 2–4%.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” (neutral), model tends to drift toward recent low; avoid over-optimistic forecasts; anchor to 14-day moving average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates near-term volatility; cap forecast variance at ±3% of 14-day moving average to avoid extreme outliers.
